---
title: Converting a document with q2 convert
---

## Overview

`q2 convert` turns a document into another representation. One conversion
exists today: a `.qmd` file becomes a notebook that
[Positron](https://positron.posit.co) can read as its cache of inline outputs.
With that notebook in place, Positron shows the outputs of your cells without
running them again.

```bash
q2 convert report.qmd --to positron-ipynb -o report.ipynb
```

The output format is always explicit: `--to` has no default and is never
guessed from the name given to `-o`. The notebook is built from the
document's [execution record](execution-records.qmd), so the command may run
your code to produce one; [Where the record comes from](#where-the-record-comes-from)
explains when.

## Options

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--to positron-ipynb` | The output format. Required. |
| `--from qmd` | The input format. Optional: `.qmd` and `.md` files are read as `qmd`. |
| `-o <path>` | Where to write the notebook. Required. `-o -` writes it to standard output. |
| `-M 'key: value'` | Sets document metadata for this run, as in `q2 render -M`. |
| `--source-uri <uri>` | The location written into the notebook as `quarto_source`. |

By default `quarto_source` is the absolute path of the document, written with
forward slashes. Pass `--source-uri` when the notebook will be read on a
machine where that path does not exist.

An existing output file is overwritten, and the command prints a note when it
does so. The `--to ipynb` and `--from ipynb` conversions are reserved names:
they exit with a usage error until they are implemented.

## Where the record comes from

The command first looks for the copy of the record that
[`record: true`](execution-records.qmd#keeping-a-copy-of-the-record) leaves
under `.quarto/`. When there is none, it runs the document to produce one,
which executes your code.

The `execute: record-sources` key controls this choice. For `q2 convert` it
accepts two entries, and its default is `q2,engine`:

| Entry | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `q2` | Use the copy under `.quarto/execution-records/`. |
| `engine` | Run the document when there is no copy. |

Set the key in the document's front matter, or for a single run with `-M`.
With `q2` alone, the command never runs the document:

```bash
q2 convert report.qmd --to positron-ipynb -o report.ipynb \
  -M 'execute:{record-sources: q2}'
```

If no copy exists, this exits with code 10 instead of executing anything.
Other entries, such as `cache`, are ignored with an info line.

The command does not check whether the copy under `.quarto/` is out of date
with the document. Render the document again with `record: true` first if
you have edited it since.

## What the command prints

On success, the command prints one line of JSON, to standard output. With
`-o -` the notebook takes standard output and the JSON line goes to standard
error instead. The line reports the cells it wrote and the cells it left out:

```json
{"cells":4,"dropped":[],"skipped":[{"id":"0-f2bd0a9f-inline","reason":"inline unit"}]}
```

`cells` counts the cells in the notebook. Each entry of `skipped` names a unit
that could not be represented, with the reason: inline expressions, for
example, have no cell in Positron's cache. Diagnostics go to standard error.

The notebook holds the outputs the record holds, whatever engine produced
them: Jupyter, Julia and knitr documents all convert. A cell with
`results: hide` or `results: asis` keeps its output in the file; how Positron
displays such an output is up to Positron.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The notebook was written. |
| 2 | A usage error, such as a missing `-o` or an unsupported pair of formats. |
| 10 | There is no record, and the record sources do not allow running the document. |
| 11 | The record has no cells that can be exported. The JSON line is still printed. |
| 12 | The record is unreadable or invalid. |
| 13 | Running the document failed. A cell that raises an error fails the run; set `#| error: true` on the cell or `execute: error: true` to keep going and export the error output. |
